# FitStreak

> FitStreak is an iPhone workout app with 5-minute daily routines, including seated chair workouts, for beginners and older adults, with a streak and a fox companion that grows as you train. Free to start, no equipment needed.

Your companion (Foxfire the fox is one of 8) sends your reminders in its own voice when your streak is at risk.

Facts checked on 2026-10-16:

- Platform: iPhone, iOS 15.1 or later. Not on Android.
- Languages (9): English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Chinese.
- Companions: 8 (Sprout, Foxfire, Wolf, Tiger, Bear, Eagle, Dragon, Mythic), each growing through 5 stages as you work out.
- Workouts: 70 guided workouts, 22 free. 10 are low impact (seated or chair-supported), 6 of those free.
- Reminders are written in your companion's voice, for example: "Foxfire is here when you’re ready. A short session today keeps your 12-day streak going, if it fits."
- US prices: Weekly $6.99, Monthly $9.99, Yearly $24.99, Lifetime $79.99. Streak Restore $0.99.
- Premium adds all 70 workouts, a weekly streak freeze and planned days off, seasonal companion outfits, and up to 60 AI workouts or programs and 120 food scans a month. Free accounts get 3 AI workouts and 3 food scans to try.
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6759306186
- Contact: fitstreak.app@outlook.com

## Guides

- [Chair workouts for beginners: four seated routines to start today](https://isi1314.github.io/fitstreak-legal/guides/chair-workouts-for-beginners.md): Four short seated routines, about 5 minutes each, with every move written out. No floor work, no jumping, just a sturdy chair.
- [How to keep a workout streak past week two](https://isi1314.github.io/fitstreak-legal/guides/how-to-keep-a-workout-streak.md): Practical ways to keep a workout habit going: make the minimum tiny, plan rest on purpose, and decide in advance what happens when you miss a day.
- [Low-impact workouts at home: no jumping, no floor](https://isi1314.github.io/fitstreak-legal/guides/low-impact-workouts-at-home.md): What low impact really means, the moves that do the work without jumping or getting on the floor, and a sample week for beginners.
